📡 Exclusive | Media reports on consultation with Qatari mediator ‘baseless speculations’: Baqaei

📌 New York, IRNA – Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei has dismissed as ‘baseless speculations’ some media reports regarding Iran’s diplomatic consultation with the Qatari mediator in New York.

Speaking to an IRNA reporter late on Monday, Baqaei made the clarification regarding published reports on Iran–US negotiations were merely speculations, noting that such accounts had no basis in reality.
​
He acknowledged that a meeting took place on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly between Iranian and Qatari delegations in the afternoon, in which the mediator’s views and assessments were received, alongside discussions on the latest regional developments.
​
Baqaei stated that the Iranian side also conveyed its observations to the Qatari counterpart, emphasizing the Islamic Republic’s resoluteness and steadfastness in defending its national interests against any excessive demands or aggression, similar to its consistent participation in diplomatic processes in good faith.
​
Last week, Iran explicitly set out its conditions to the United States for resuming the diplomatic process in indirect messages through the Qatari mediator.
​
The conditions included a halt to US acts of aggression — including the maritime blockade and economic terrorism — an end to the war on all fronts, the release of frozen assets, and acceptance of safe shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, as agreed upon between the two littoral states of Iran and Oman.

📡 Iranian diplomat rejects Canadian FM’s allegations at UN

📌 New York, IRNA – Iran’s representative to the United Nations General Assembly has rejected allegations by Canada’s foreign minister, saying that Western countries spread disinformation to shield Israel from accountability for its crimes.

Nasser Asadi, Third Counsellor at Iran’s Permanent Mission to the UN in New York, made the remarks on Monday in response to the Canadian foreign minister’s speech at the UNGA, in which she described Iran as the main threat to regional peace and security.
​
Asadi said the real insult to international law was the desperate attempt to whitewash Israel’s crimes through disinformation, diverting public attention, demonizing a country and labeling it the so-called “main threat to peace and security.”
​
He described as the “biggest lie of the century” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s characterization of the genocide in Gaza as the “biggest lie of the century” during his address to the UN General Assembly last week.
​
The Iranian diplomat stressed that neither Netanyahu’s remarks nor those of Canada’s foreign minister could erase documented facts, invalidate court findings and rulings, whitewash crimes witnessed by the world, or change Israel’s status as the “main threat to peace and security.”
​
Asadi further said that no fabrication or falsehood could absolve Canada or other Western countries, particularly the United States, of their international responsibilities.
​
He added that these countries could not escape the individual criminal responsibility of their officials for involvement in crimes committed by Israel in the West Asia region.
